messages:
alex: hey @people-ops :wave: quick q — need to add my dad to benefits. He's been placed under court-ordered conservatorship (effective 2026-03-02). Open enroll closed. Is conservatorship a QLE? What docs do you need and can coverage be retroactive? also worried about payroll/proration and HSA implications.

Maya (People Ops): hi alex — sorry to hear that. Conservatorship can qualify as a QLE since it changes dependent status. We'll need a few docs to process: 1) court appointment/order showing the conservatorship and effective date; 2) proof of relationship or residency (utility bill, SSN letter, or gov ID); 3) current insurance docs if the dependent had other coverage (medicare/medicaid or private). Please upload via the benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.example/upload and choose "QLE - Conservatorship". Normal deadline is 30 days from event date; we can escalate exceptions with supporting docs. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks — the court order is dated 2026-03-02. if we submit today, what would the effective date be? and how does retro billing work?

Sam (Benefits): if approved, medical/dental/vision can be backdated to the conservatorship effective date (3/2/2026). HSA note: adding a dependent doesn't automatically disqualify HSA eligibility, but it may change whether you are considered self-only vs family coverage for contribution limits — we'll confirm based on the plan you enroll in. also, if your dad is on Medicare that can affect primary/secondary status — include proof of that so we can coordinate. :mag:

Raj (Payroll): heads-up on payroll side — premiums are billed retroactively. we'll calculate prorated premiums from 3/2 to the next payroll. retro premium will typically be collected on the next paycheck; if the dollar amount is large we can spread the adjustment across the next 2 pay cycles if you select that option in the upload form. note the payroll cut-off for adjustments is 48hrs before pay processing.

alex: will I get id cards right away? and if he has medicare/medicaid does that block enrollment entirely?

Sam (Benefits): we issue digital ID cards within 48 hours of activation; physical cards ship in 7-10 business days. if your dad has Medicare Part A/B, Medicare often becomes primary for those benefits — that may make employer coverage secondary or in some cases unnecessary; but we still need the docs to determine coordination of benefits. if he's only on Medicaid we can usually enroll him, but include current insurance letters.

Maya (People Ops): steps for you: 1) gather the court order + proof docs, 2) upload to the portal and choose "QLE - Conservatorship", 3) indicate requested effective date (3/2/2026) and payroll adjustment preference (one-time vs spread), 4) add a short note if immediate medical care is required. we'll triage submissions in ~3 business days; if anything's missing we'll reach out here. cc @Raj @Sam. :thumbsup:

BenefitsBot: Reminder — QLE uploads require timestamped/legal documents. incomplete submissions will be auto-closed after 7 days.

alex: uploaded just now (conservatorship_order_20260302.pdf, proof_residency_mar2026.jpg). thanks all.

Maya (People Ops): got the upload — i'll review and route to benefits for approval. ETA 48-72 hrs. i'll post updates in this thread.

Raj (Payroll): noted. if benefits approve by friday we'll plan to collect retro premium on the 3/20 paycheck. i'll confirm exact amount once benefits posts the effective date.

alex: appreciate it. one last q — does adding a dependent change my HSA contribution limits mid-year? i'm planning contributions for the year.

Sam (Benefits): good question — HSA contribution limits depend on whether you're enrolled in self-only or family HDHP coverage. if you switch from individual to family HDHP when adding a dependent, your max contribution allowance may change pro rata for the year. we'll confirm the plan election and, if needed, send an HSA adjustment form to update your elections.

Maya (People Ops): looping back — if you don't hear from us in 72 hours ping me here and i'll escalate. sending well wishes to you and your family. :pray:
